45.mount: breadboard forward of seat (same as sessions 37/42)
45.conditions: glassy, no waves, strong tidal current, some wind
45.notes: Third on-water test, OC paddle. Forgot SESSION_END but data is clean (0 CRC errors, 0 resync bytes, 0 ts underflows; duration taken from IMU timestamps). 17 TIME records -> time-record alignment. KG ran 82.7 min; Garmin/SpeedCoach cover 53.8 min and started ~893 s (14.9 min) into the KG log (paddled out with KG running). SpeedCoach was in 'Just Go' mode = ONE interval (1919 strokes, avg 41 spm): gives per-stroke ground truth but NO interval/lap structure; lap structure comes from 15 Garmin manual lap presses. Lap roles confirmed from data: L1 = 1-min drift calibration (0 strokes, dead-still); L2 = ~9-min steady warmup at pace (no build-up); L3 and L4 = the two sprint BUILD-UPS (force 33->55 / 31->44 lbs, cadence ~37->55 spm, speed ramps to 6.5 mph within the piece); L5-L9 = short pieces; L6/L11 = near-rest transitions; L10 (14 min) and L13 (10 min) = long steady distance pieces; L15 = flying-the-ama balance drill (near-stationary 10 m, 22 light SpeedCoach strokes, heel held ~+1.9 deg off float baseline, roll-rate RMS 0.25 rad/s = 2.4x cruise). SpeedCoach cross-check: KG-vs-SC instantaneous speed r=0.954, per-lap mean speed median |diff| 0.04 mph, KG counted 1751/1919 strokes (91%). LEG-DRIVE A/B confirmed by paddler durations (no-leg pieces shorter ~50 s, leg pieces longer); paddler did RIGHT side first this session: L6 = RIGHT no-leg (46 s), L7 = RIGHT leg (66 s), L8 = LEFT no-leg (51 s), L9 = LEFT leg (58 s). The leg-drive signal is NOT in raw peak force, impulse, connection%, or yaw-side-bias (~50% on every lap), but IS clear in WORK PER STROKE from the force-vs-distance curve (area under drive force vs boat travel): RIGHT 71->125 J (+76%, via a fuller/longer arch = textbook sustained leg connection), LEFT 94->147 J (+56%, via a higher peak ~33->50 lbf = hit harder rather than longer). Within-pair contrast is clean because the pair laps are adjacent in time/conditions; absolute J is boat-response, not blade force. Blind whole-lap scans wash this out by mixing sides/efforts. L12 was a light-paddling experiment (barely moving, sometimes just dipping the blade) to watch how the SpeedCoach detects strokes -- NOT a real piece, so it is excluded. gap_fill_strokes=true recovers soft real strokes the amplitude detector drops on moving cruise pieces (cadence-guided; no effect on rests/drills).

42.paddle: dragon-boat paddle (note: session 37 used an OC paddle)
42.mount: breadboard forward of seat (identical to session 37)
42.conditions: flat, mostly glass water, light tidal current, calm
42.notes: Second on-water test. Dragon-boat paddle (not OC). No 30 s static calibration performed. Workout: ~10 min warmup (lap 1), continuous ~2 min efforts ~9:45-30 min (laps 2-13), then structured set 2x2 min, 6x1 min, 8x30 s pieces alternating sides, started right. Lap structure is 4 presses per cycle: paddle one side -> lap -> REST -> lap -> paddle other side -> lap -> REST -> lap. So in the structured set every other lap is a REST (~50-90 m, ~0 strokes) and is auto-skipped (<10 strokes); the work pieces are the laps with strokes. LEFT-side pieces intentionally weak (finger pain), progressively weaker through the session; cleanest L/R contrast is the 6x1 min block (laps 19-29). NOTE laps 30 (404 s) and 46 (185 s) are long rests/transitions that still contain slow strokes, so don't assume strict work/rest parity past lap 29. 46 Garmin manual lap presses. Garmin export is FIT (sport=stand_up_paddleboarding). SpeedCoach to be added later. Firmware has TIME records -> time-record alignment (xcorr validation r=0.959).

37.notes: First on-water test. Wave 1 + Wave 2 firmware. No TIME records (pre-2026-05-23 firmware).
summary_narrative: Current estimate ~1.2 mph each way (rough — assumes similar effort both directions). L2 ran 6.7 mph with current, L13 ran 4.3 mph against. Cadences matched (~48 spm) but force differed ~10% (46.4 vs 42.0 lbs), so part of the 2.4 mph gap is real effort variation, not just current. A drift test or NOAA tidal data would tighten this.
Connected stroke % drops in chop. Glass water L13 = 18%, choppy fast laps L2-3 = 6-9%. Same paddler, same cadence — water conditions disrupt catch timing.
Pull is brief (~0.45 s), glide is the dominant phase (~0.75 s). Higher cadence shrinks glide time, not pull time — there's less recovery to set up the next catch.
